name: Iso-Lateral Low Row
source: Official Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Low Row demonstration video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k2S4G14cmts, 25.3s-26.5s, 4 side-view frames f_006, f_008, f_010, f_012). Single-arm near workarm modeled with 55 lb (24.95 kg) added plates (1x45 lb + 1x10 lb); slight 3D arc divergence introduces ~4-6% projection uncertainty.

observation.evidence: Official Hammer Strength Plate-Loaded Iso-Lateral Low Row demonstration video (YouTube ID k2S4G14cmts, static level side view at 25.3s-26.5s; frames f_006.jpg, f_008.jpg, f_010.jpg, f_012.jpg at 6 fps from 24.5s). Modeled assembly is the near-side (left) independent rigid lever arm pivoting counterclockwise in the side view around the upper-front bearing housing. Added load on the moving upper horn is one 45 lb plate plus one 10 lb plate (55 lb = 24.95 kg); the lower 45 lb plate sits on a fixed storage horn. Grip is the athlete's left hand on the lower handle. Slight 3D arc divergence of the iso-lateral arm and near-top framing of the plate horn at full contraction introduce minor projection uncertainty (~4-6%). Compound multi-joint horizontal pull; anatomical joint fields omitted.

base_resistance.source: Hammer Strength specifies 8 lbs (3.6 kg) starting resistance per arm for the Plate-Loaded Iso-Lateral Low Row (IL-LR). Its variation across travel is unknown; the default holds this force constant.
